### Summary

A face flux in snapy is not a private array of the code that computes it. The register owns, for each active
direction, one tensor of face fluxes, the stage total; the Riemann solve writes it, and later producers (the
sources, the limiters) add to it or scale it in place. Routing every write through a few register calls is what
lets the register keep wall faces prescribed, keep copies of named parts, and know that a direction changed.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Write a direction's stage total in place: the first producer's slot, then plain row adds and in-place
scales, in call order ([-@eq-ch10-posts-add]).

**Data.** $\mathbf T_d$, rows by faces, in the flux storage dtype; a post is a flux density per unit face area and
time, before stage weights.

**Placement.** Inside a stage, between `begin_stage` and `end_stage`.

**Activation.** Always; no switch.

**Guarantee / limits.** The adds round exactly as successive in-place adds of the same increments.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of this section.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathbf T_d$ is the stage total of direction  \in \{1, 2, 3\}$, a tensor of rows by faces;
$\mathbf q$ is one producer's increment for a list of rows; $\phi$ is a scale factor. Every write marks direction
$ as written (@sec-ch10-prescribed).

### Derivation

No equation beyond bookkeeping. For a list of rows , \dots, r_m$ and an increment $\mathbf q$ with $ rows,
an add is

2330
\mathbf T_d[r_k] \leftarrow \mathbf T_d[r_k] + \mathbf q[k], \qquad k = 1, \dots, m,
2330 {#eq-ch10-posts-add}

The add is {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::add >}}.

done in call order and never fused with another producer's add. A scale multiplies the rows in place,
$\mathbf T_d[r_k] \leftarrow \phi\,\mathbf T_d[r_k]$, with $\phi$ either one factor for every row or one per row.
Floating-point addition is not associative, so the order is part of the result: two producers that add in the
same order give the same bits on every device.

### Numerical method

The first post of a stage is the slot: `slot` returns $\mathbf T_d$ itself, the producer writes it, and
`post_slot` records its name. An add whose rows are contiguous is one in-place add on a row range; other row lists
add row by row. No scatter-add is used: on CUDA a scatter-add of FP64 rows adds atomically, so its result can depend
on thread order, and the captured stage must equal the eager one bitwise. A part that a reader requested at reset
(a kept part) receives a copy of the increment of the producer with the same name. @fig-ch10-register-order shows
where the posts fall in a stage.

```{python}

#| fig-cap: "The register's writes in one stage, in order: the posts, the prescribed-face apply before the divergence, the apply after the implicit correction, the wall batch's flush and the end of the stage, which folds the stage total into the step field."
#| fig-alt: "A vertical list of seven steps, each with a coloured marker and a one-line description, connected by arrows from begin_stage down to end_stage."
```

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| the first post | {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::slot >}} | `slot` | none |
| record the slot's name | {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::post_slot >}} | `post_slot` | none |
| row adds | {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::add >}} | `add` | none |

| kept parts | {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::kept >}} | `kept` | none |

: The code of the posts. {#tbl-ch10-posts-code}

Walk-through: `add` checks that the increment has as many rows as the list, marks the direction, and either adds
on one row range (contiguous rows) or adds row by row; a kept part of the same name is overwritten with the
increment. `scale` marks the direction and multiplies each listed row. An increment with the wrong number of rows
stops with an error that names the producer.

### Limits

The adds are exact only as bookkeeping: the result depends on the order of the producers, which the stage fixes.
A producer that writes $\mathbf T_d$ directly, without `add` or `scale`, does not mark the direction; the implicit
correction does this and is handled by its own apply (@sec-ch10-prescribed). Switch combinations are in
@sec-ch12-matrix.
